lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count the kids who say no.

lines.text: Here's the question.

lines.text: In a class of twenty-four kids,

lines.text: Twenty kids like pizza,

lines.text: Eighteen kids like pasta,

lines.text: and sixteen like soup. What is the smallest possible number of kids who like all three?

lines.text: So what do we know? Twenty-four kids, and three counts: twenty, eighteen and sixteen.
lines.caption: So what do we know? Twenty-four kids, and three counts: twenty, eighteen and sixteen.

lines.text: We want the smallest POSSIBLE number who like all three.
lines.caption: We want the smallest POSSIBLE number who like all three.

lines.text: So we get to arrange who likes what, and try to make that group as small as we can.
lines.caption: So we get to arrange who likes what, and try to make that group as small as we can.

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: count the kids who say no.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: count the kids who say no.

lines.text: Twenty like pizza, so four kids don't.
lines.caption: Twenty like pizza, so four kids don't.

lines.text: Eighteen like pasta, so six don't. Sixteen like soup, so eight don't.
lines.caption: Eighteen like pasta, so six don't. Sixteen like soup, so eight don't.

lines.text: Any kid who says no to even one food is NOT in the all-three group.
lines.caption: Any kid who says no to even one food is NOT in the all-three group.

lines.text: To make the all-three group small, give the no's to different kids. No kid says no twice.
lines.caption: To make the all-three group small, give the no's to different kids. No kid says no twice.

lines.text: Then four plus six plus eight is eighteen kids who say no to something.
lines.caption: Then four plus six plus eight is eighteen kids who say no to something.

lines.text: That leaves twenty-four minus eighteen, six kids who say no to nothing. They like all three!
lines.caption: That leaves twenty-four minus eighteen, six kids who say no to nothing. They like all three!

lines.text: Check the counts: twenty like pizza, eighteen like pasta, sixteen like soup. It works.
lines.caption: Check the counts: twenty like pizza, eighteen like pasta, sixteen like soup. It works.

lines.text: And we can't do better, because there are only eighteen no's to hand out.
lines.caption: And we can't do better, because there are only eighteen no's to hand out.

lines.text: The answer is six. That's Choice C!
lines.caption: The answer is six. That's Choice C!

lines.text: Here's another way: combine two foods at a time.

lines.text: Pizza and pasta: twenty plus eighteen is thirty-eight.
lines.caption: Pizza and pasta: twenty plus eighteen is thirty-eight.

lines.text: That's fourteen more than twenty-four, so at least fourteen kids like both.
lines.caption: That's fourteen more than twenty-four, so at least fourteen kids like both.

lines.text: Now add soup. Fourteen plus sixteen is thirty.
lines.caption: Now add soup. Fourteen plus sixteen is thirty.

lines.text: That's six more than twenty-four, so at least six like all three. Same answer!
lines.caption: That's six more than twenty-four, so at least six like all three. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When you want to see the overlap shrink one food at a time.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice B, four, is the number of kids who don't like pizza. That's only one of the counts.

lines.caption: Choice D, fourteen, is the pizza and pasta overlap. That's what you get if you stop before adding soup.

lines.text: Choice A, zero, would need twenty-four no's. There are only eighteen, so six kids must like everything.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. To find the smallest group that says yes to everything, count the no's.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now there are four things to like.

lines.caption: Give them to different kids: five plus eight plus ten plus three is twenty-six no's in all.

lines.text: Thirty minus twenty-six is four. At least four kids like all four!
lines.caption: Thirty minus twenty-six is four. At least four kids like all four!

lines.text: Here's the cool part. A fourth favorite didn't make it harder, just one more count.
lines.caption: Here's the cool part. A fourth favorite didn't make it harder, just one more count.

lines.text: If you got four, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Count how many kids say no to each thing, and give the no's to different kids.
